item.title: Scientists are turning seawater into a ‘blood test’ that could reveal coral reef damage before it becomes visible
item.description: Researchers are using water chemistry and microbes to monitor coral reef health. Ocean currents significantly influence these chemical and microbial patterns. This approach mirrors human medicine's early disease detection methods. It allows for detecting changes before visible stress appears on corals. This interdisciplinary work aims to protect vital ocean ecosystems.

item.title: A 17-year-old student proposed a hybrid nuclear energy system that could reduce an Antarctic base's carbon emissions by 3,254 tons annually
item.description: A young Chilean student has proposed an innovative energy system for Antarctica. This concept combines renewable sources with a nuclear microreactor for reliable power. The system aims to significantly reduce diesel fuel dependence and carbon emissions. It offers a potential solution for powering remote research stations in extreme conditions. This student-led idea highlights future possibilities for sustainable Antarctic energy.

item.title: Will Smith once used this $2.5 million, 1,200-square-foot motorhome on film sets; the two-storey vehicle is now a luxury stay near Austin: Why it remains so special
item.description: Will Smith's custom-built luxury motorhome, 'The Heat,' is now available for rent. This impressive 53-foot double-decker RV offers extensive living space and advanced features. It previously served Smith during major film productions like 'Ali' and 'Suicide Squad.' The motorhome now anchors a glamping resort outside Austin, Texas. Guests can experience a taste of Hollywood luxury at a significantly reduced price.

item.title: Scientists capture first wild footage of rare Arctic squid with its eggs
item.description: Scientists documented a rare Arctic bobtail squid guarding its eggs in Northeast Greenland. This marks the first confirmed in situ record of Rossia moelleri in its natural habitat. The observation occurred in the world's largest national park, a remote Arctic fjord. This finding fills a gap in understanding Arctic cephalopods and their reproduction. It provides a baseline for tracking marine life in a rapidly warming Arctic region.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Quote of the day by Socrates: ‘Beware the barrenness of a busy life,’ and why constant activity can leave little room for a meaningful life
item.description: Modern societies often equate busyness with achievement and productivity. This perspective contrasts with ancient Greek philosophy which valued leisure for thought. Constant activity can reduce concentration and hinder learning and creativity. Meaningful experiences require time for reflection and appreciation of what matters. A life rich in meaning is not necessarily the busiest one.

item.title: Quote of the day by Kobe Bryant: "I don't want to be the next Michael Jordan, I only want to be…" - a timeless lesson on authenticity, self-belief and creating your own legacy
item.description: Kobe Bryant famously stated he only wanted to be Kobe Bryant, not the next Michael Jordan. This quote highlights the importance of self-belief and avoiding living in another's shadow. Bryant studied great players but focused on developing his unique strengths and game. Constant comparison can hinder personal growth and obscure individual talents. Authenticity and self-belief ultimately lead to lasting impact and individual success.

item.title: California eradicated these 20-pound rodents decades ago; DNA suggests someone deliberately brought them back
item.description: California believed nutria were eradicated, but they reappeared in the Central Valley. A new genetic study indicates these rodents were reintroduced by humans. Nutria damage wetlands and weaken vital flood control structures. Their feeding and burrowing habits cause significant ecological and agricultural harm. This discovery highlights the critical need for prevention alongside removal efforts.

item.title: Scientists find 30% of catfish population in Vermont lake affected by a transmissible cancer
item.description: A groundbreaking study has unveiled a new transmissible cancer affecting catfish populations, characterized by skin lesions that can spread from one fish to another, which is an unusual occurrence in the animal kingdom. Researchers are now delving into the mechanisms of this disease's transmission, which has already affected numerous lakes throughout New England and Canada, placing catfish among a rare group of animals susceptible to transmissible cancers.

item.title: Billionaire Steve Wynn's Beverly Hills estate sells for $47.75M after five years on the market
item.description: Billionaire Steve Wynn's Beverly Hills mansion has finally sold for $47.75 million. The lavish estate, known as Villa Lulu, was on the market for over five years. After extensive renovations and price adjustments, the property found a buyer. This sale highlights challenges in the ultra-luxury real estate market. The transaction concludes a significant chapter in Los Angeles' high-end property sales.

item.title: Burkina Faso tightens gold mining control; official gold worth $6 billion recorded
item.description: Burkina Faso recorded more than$6 billion worth of goldthrough official channels in the first half of 2026 after producing and procuring over55 tonnes of gold. The military-led government says its mining reforms aim to bring more artisanal gold into the formal economy, reduce smuggling, improve transparency and increase state revenue. It has also expanded mining oversight, formed new cooperatives and continued investments in electricity infrastructure.

item.title: Workers building dam uncover 15th-century burials in Angola before flooding submerged them
item.description: Archaeologists excavating a site in central Angola before it is flooded by a hydroelectric dam have uncovered the country's oldest radiocarbon-dated burials, earliest known stone structures and only known ancient urn cremation. Dating to the early 1400s, the discoveries provide new evidence of organised communities and burial traditions before European arrival.

item.description: Villa Skyfall, a stunning estate available for $85 million in Delray Beach, Florida, epitomizes luxury living. item.title: After World War II, a few snakes reached Guam; they now number up to 30,000 per square mile, and scientists found 19,000 hidden genetic changes
item.description: Brown tree snakes invaded Guam after World War II, causing ecological damage. These snakes now exist in extremely high densities across the island. New research reveals thousands of hidden DNA changes in the snakes. This genetic flexibility helps them adapt to new environments and survive. The findings challenge previous understandings of invasive species and inbreeding.
